c. Project Geology and Groundwater
(1) Geology
A survey of the geological characteristics of the project area was conducted by the Environmental Geology Division, Bureau of Topographic and Geologic Survey, Department of Environmental Resources, Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. This Survey contained the following description of these characteristics:
"The bedrock is overlain by loose rock materials consisting of silt, sand and gravel. This mantle of unconsolidated material is variable in thickness; twenty-five (25) feet would probably be a maximum thickness.
The bedrock is broken with closely-spaced fractures (breaks in the rocks) and is steeply titled to the south. In general, the bedrock distribution from north to south in the area of interest is as follows:
1. Woodbine Street to a point between Harris and Boyd Streets is underlain by interbedded dark gray shale, siltstone, sandstone and conglomerate. When these rocks (except for the sandstone) are exposed to the atmosphere they weather (deteriorate) rapidly and deeply.
2. Point between Harris and Boyd Streets to Cumberland Street is underlain by black shale, limestone and dolomite. These rocks are usually well bedded and the fracturing is not as well developed as they are described in (1) above. The rocks are moderately resistant to weathering.
Most of these rocks are covered by roads, buildings, parking lots and other works of man; thus, the recharge potential in the area is low. Usually the carbonate rocks (limestone and dolomite of rock (2) described above) show better ground water production characteristics than the interbedded shales, siltstones, sandstones, and conglomerates."
